name: European Media Freedom Act
evidence_rating: ex-ante only: Act fully applicable since Aug 2025; only baseline monitoring data
summary: The Commission forecast that the Media Freedom Act would lift media companies' revenues by about EUR 2.9 billion a year and reduce risks to editorial independence. The Act has only applied in full since August 2025; the new EU media board is operating, but the Media Pluralism Monitor's latest results describe the situation before the Act and use a new scale. No study has yet measured its effects.

indicators.indicator: Number and value of cross-border investments in EU media markets (annual)
indicators.target_or_baseline: Baseline 2013-2021: 478 EU and 389 non-EU investor transactions; gradual increase expected

indicators.indicator: Board opinions taken into account; share of cases solved by the Board; number of guidance documents
indicators.evidence: European Board for Media Services set up in 2025 and adopted its first reports and deliverables (Dec 2025 plenary); no data on uptake of opinions found.

indicators.indicator: Media Pluralism Monitor risk scores on political independence, PSM governance, owner influence, source protection, ownership transparency
indicators.evidence: MPM2025 (2024 data) published, but switched to a six-tier scale so results are not strictly comparable with earlier editions; it covers the period before EMFA fully applied (Aug 2025).

indicators.indicator: Citizens' trust in media; number of Member States with media self-regulatory bodies
Net economic benefit (higher media company revenues)
indicators.evidence: Not evaluated; first evaluation due four years after entry into force.

literature.citation: European Commission (2022), Impact Assessment accompanying the European Media Freedom Act proposal (executive summary SWD(2022) 287), SWD(2022) 286
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the European Media Freedom Act proposal (executive summary SWD(2022) 287)
literature.outcomes: media revenues; compliance costs; regulator costs
literature.headline: Annual net economic benefits EUR 2.9bn in higher media revenues; one-off business costs EUR 9.4-14m and recurrent EUR 5.6-14.5m; public authority costs EUR 6.1m a year
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected the Act to raise media companies' revenues by about EUR 2.9 billion a year, at negligible cost to businesses.

literature.citation: Blagojev, Bleyer-Simon, Brogi, Carlini, Da Costa Leite Borges, Kermer, Nenadic, Palmer, Parcu, Reviglio, Trevisan & Verza (2025), Monitoring media pluralism in the European Union: results of the MPM2025, EUI Centre for Media Pluralism and Media Freedom, RSC Research Report (doi:10.2870/2415644)
literature.authors: Blagojev, Bleyer-Simon, Brogi, Carlini, Da Costa Leite Borges, Kermer, Nenadic, Palmer, Parcu, Reviglio, Trevisan & Verza
literature.title: Monitoring media pluralism in the European Union: results of the MPM2025
literature.venue: EUI Centre for Media Pluralism and Media Freedom, RSC Research Report (doi:10.2870/2415644)
literature.outcomes: media pluralism; editorial independence; ownership transparency
literature.headline: Risk assessment for 2024 across 32 countries, with insights on EMFA-related themes before the Act fully applied; new six-tier scale not strictly comparable with earlier years
literature.summary_plain: The EU-funded Media Pluralism Monitor gives a pre-EMFA baseline of risks to media freedom; commentary on it describes uneven readiness to apply the Act.
literature.interested_party: Centre is co-financed by the EU and its MPM is the Act's own monitoring indicator source
